name: vrooli-memory.scope-bootstrap
purpose: Create a scenario's usage memory scope with its facet vocabulary and starter classification rules, idempotently, and report what already existed.

label.description: Human label; defaults to the scope id.

facets.description: Facet vocabulary. NOT settable through the binding today (manifest bind_waiver on facets-json); when the scope does not exist and facets are given, the program returns partial/facets_not_settable and the caller creates the scope with the CLI first.

rules.description: Starter rules: [{id, facet, body_pattern, kind?, priority?}]. Created disabled, dry-run, enabled only when the dry run matched at least one entry or the corpus is empty.

assumptions: vrooli-memory is running; a degraded health (embeddings) still accepts scope and rule writes
the caller owns the scope name and is not bootstrapping another scenario's scope
each call runs in its own program-runtime session; session variables persist across submissions
invariants: the only writes are scopes/create, rules/create, and rules/enable, each declared below
an existing scope is never re-created; its budgets are left as they are
a rule is never enabled without a dry run in the same submission
the envelope is printed exactly once, on every path
a scope that does not exist is created without facets, or not at all when facets were requested

signals.scope_existed: true when the scope was already registered
signals.scope_created: true when this run created it
signals.rules: list of {id, existed, created, dry_run_matches, enabled}
signals.facets: the facet vocabulary in effect (as requested when created; unknown when pre-existing)

fixtures.note: fixture-only scope: never point a fixture at a live usage scope
